public_rationale: McKinsey's contemporary survey documents businesses experiencing consequential inaccuracies and growing recognition of that risk. This supports the ordinary reading that businesses were discovering practical limitations. The same report records benefits, so it does not support the surrounding suggestion that generative AI was generally useless.
limitations: The evidence does not establish that most businesses experienced harm or that most outputs were erroneous.
The primary report was read through an externally hosted copy; available_at refers to the original report's publication.
The business-benefit findings in e1 limit the broader negative interpretation but do not contradict recognition of errors.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Businesses are discovering that generative AI tools have major limitations and are riddled with errors.

statement.excerpt: Businesses are finally finding this out, too.
statement.document_title: The need for a President that speaks AI natively

from_speaker: Businesses are finally finding this out, too.
AI Work Assistants Need a Lot of Handholding
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that businesses using generative AI were encountering substantial errors and recognizing its limitations. It does not require every business to agree or establish that the technology has no value.
For this ongoing observation, use early-to-mid-2024 business experience reported before the June 28 post: January 1 through June 28, 2024.
Read 'finally' as increasing practical recognition, rather than a claim that no business previously understood these risks.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary business surveys or documented deployments show that businesses encountered consequential inaccuracies and increasingly recognized limitations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evidence shows that substantial inaccuracies were uncommon and that businesses were not encountering the described limitations.
